title: Chasing Market Growth and Matching Performance in Two-Sided Platforms: Evidence from the Lazy-Minting Policy in an NFT Marketplace
eligible_reason: Single adoption date: the lazy-minting policy was introduced on one platform (Rarible, treated_platform = 1) at one date, with Foundation as the control platform; treatment = treated_platform x after. The NFT-level repeated cross-section has platform FE and creation-day FE only (two groups, one switch date), and most columns add NFT-level covariates (sale_type item_type). The headline matching outcome (first_match) is estimated by conditional logit/probit. de Chaisemartin-D'Haultfoeuille (did_multiplegt_old) and drdid are run as appendix robustness, but on the same one-cohort design. Fails the at-least-two-adoption-cohorts rule.
design_notes: replication_data.dta: 1.3M NFTs created on Rarible and Foundation, Aug 16 2021 - Feb 7 2022. Table 2: clogit first_match (group(day)) and reghdfe log_first_sale_price treatment sale_type item_type, absorb(treated_platform day) vce(cluster day), full sample and gas-minted (lazy_minted==0) subsample. Event-study version with pre_55..post_55 relative-week dummies. Creator-level creations panel (creator x date FE). Bidder-week panels (bidder + week FE). CEM-matched sample, mediation (medeff), multihomer and SuperRare robustness. Appendix: did_multiplegt_old (lines 411-426 of replication_code.do), drdid (lines 435-438), Stuart (2014) weighting.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: One treated platform (Rarible) switching at a single policy date.
data_access_note: Collected from public Rarible/Foundation APIs; all datasets shipped.
screener_notes: Two-platform, one-date DiD. Modern-estimator usage is cosmetic (single cohort). Not eligible.
